about.details: Runs Antigravity, Google's agent-first desktop application for software development. It needs a Google account and network access to Google's services. Its build is linked against glibc, and it was made and tried on LevitateOS. It carries the desktop runtime (GTK, NSS, X11, GLib and the C library) inside its own package instead of using the host's, so the desktop image does not have to ship them; the package is about 600 MB. Its sandbox uses unprivileged user namespaces, since the setuid helper is not installed; a kernel without them stops it with an error. The program can check for newer versions through its bundled updater; updates are made by Recipe (recipe update antigravity), and the program's own update setting can be set to manual or none. The package is proprietary Google software.
about.license: proprietary (Google terms; bundles Electron MIT, Chromium and Apache-2.0 parts)

steps.acquire: Downloads the pinned Antigravity tarball from Google's storage. Google publishes no checksum for it; the digest is of the bytes first downloaded.
steps.build: Unpacks the tarball and checks every file against its own digest; nothing is compiled.
steps.install: Puts the application under lib/antigravity without its setuid helper, adds the desktop runtime's data, rewrites the program and its libraries to the carried C library and libraries, and adds a starter, a menu entry and an icon.
